iPhone Ultra launch is just weeks away, but new reports suggest initial supply could be extremely limited, and the phone may only be available in the US at launch.

iPhone Ultra supply tight, may launch exclusively in the US first

Apple will hold an event in the US on September 8, where it will unveil its first folding iPhone — but it won't go on sale immediately. A major Chinese component supplier has confirmed that Apple is facing supply, testing, and pricing challenges, which could mean the Australian market won't see the device for several months. The supplier told ChannelNews in China that the delay is "mainly due to supply and pricing issues," adding: "We believe Apple is also encountering problems with testing of the prototypes it has produced." Australian telecom carriers and a major retailer have confirmed that the new iPhone 18 series won't appear on local retail shelves for this "Apple Fold." Due to limited supply, the product will launch first in the US, then roll out to other major markets including China.

We've already heard rumors that iPhone Ultra supply could be very tight at launch. If that's really the case, it would make sense as a short-term solution to only sell in the US first.

Although the report sounds plausible, there are reasons to remain skeptical.

Firstly, the report mentions a September 8 event, but Apple is almost certainly not picking that date.

Going with the second Tuesday has historically been a safe bet, but this year Labor Day in the US falls later, on September 7. Apple would be extremely unwise to hold an iPhone launch the day after Labor Day. Wednesday, September 9 is much more likely.

In addition, the sources for this report appear to be from China and Australia. If iPhone Ultra isn't launching in those regions soon, it makes sense that local sources would know in advance. But they may not know whether the device will be US-exclusive at launch — that claim seems more like speculation.

Regardless, it wouldn't be surprising for Apple to roll out iPhone Ultra slowly. If it can ship in the US in September and gradually add more markets, that's better than postponing the launch entirely.

When do you expect iPhone Ultra to reach users? Let us know in the comments.
